components.name: ScreenCard
components.summary: Groups one screen-related topic or task with a heading and optional explanation.
components.usage: Use within the screen detail sections for display settings, hardware, synchronization, diagnostics and management. This feature-owned composition uses native section/header markup; it does not load data, enforce permissions or own form state. Prefer the existing native link navigation for URL-owned sections rather than introducing a tab widget.
components.accessibility: The section has the supplied title as its accessible name and an h2 heading. Consumers own meaningful heading order, form labels, errors and status announcements. Uses inherited product colors for light and dark themes and collapses through the surrounding feature grid on narrow screens.

props.name: title
props.meaning: Visible heading and accessible section name.

props.name: description
props.meaning: Optional contextual guidance below the heading.

props.name: children
props.meaning: Topic-specific facts, status or caller-owned form.

props.name: className
props.meaning: Optional feature styling, such as the danger section.

states: Loading or unavailable information supplied by the caller
Danger section with a native disclosure

examples.label: Device information
examples.description: Groups reported device facts without inferring support or connection state.
examples.code: <ScreenCard title="Device and application" description="Reported by the screen."><dl><dt>App version</dt><dd>1.0.0</dd></dl></ScreenCard>

components.name: ScreenStatus
components.summary: Compact, noninteractive screen status with a decorative dot and semantic tone.
components.usage: Use in the screen list and details for pairing, connection and publication states. Keep those concepts distinct: a paired screen is not necessarily connected. The caller supplies the authorized API value and localized text; missing data stays unknown rather than appearing healthy.
components.accessibility: Always includes readable status text. Color and the decorative CSS dot are supplementary. Does not add a live region, avoiding repeated announcements from five-second polling.

props.name: tone
props.meaning: Semantic visual emphasis; does not infer business state.

examples.label: Publication failure
examples.description: The visible text explains the status independently of color.
